headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; Dify’s writable, networked orchestration can expose Chatwoot customer data and amplify unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, while Dify can ingest files and tool outputs into agent/workflow flows. A shared filesystem or copied content could let attacker-controlled text in Chatwoot be treated as instructions by Dify. The pathway is plausible but not proven by a documented direct bridge, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into Dify prompts or knowledge files
IF Dify workflows parse customer messages as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of support transcripts into agent prompts
Add a provenance tag to all imported Chatwoot text
Require a human review step before any tool call from imported content
Restrict Dify workflows to templated prompts only
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction-separation filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. Dify reads uploaded knowledge-base files, handles model-provider API keys and tool credentials, and also has broad egress. If Chatwoot data is fed into Dify, default networked processing can leak sensitive customer content outside the original support system.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records or messages are exported into Dify files or prompts
IF Dify sends those inputs to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Block customer-data uploads into Dify by default
Use a redaction step before any transfer from Chatwoot
Limit Dify to local or approved providers only
Rotate any exposed tool credentials immediately
requires-engineering: add DLP controls and per-dataset residency enforcement

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, and Dify can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write filesystems in server-side code tools. Even though Chatwoot itself is not writable, Dify can mutate shared resources or downstream artifacts while Chatwoot continues serving support data. The overlap is enough for conflicting writes or resource contention in shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate against the same workspace, database, or exported artifacts
IF Dify code tools write into paths that Chatwoot also reads or publishes
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct storage paths
Disable Dify write-capable tools for shared datasets
Add file-locking or queue-based coordination
Review any shared database or export job for race conditions
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent resource isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is explicitly an agent/workflow platform with tool wiring, so it can treat upstream outputs as authoritative unless the workflow adds verification. Chatwoot produces customer-facing support content and reports that Dify could ingest and then act on or summarize. That creates a default cascade from unverified support text into downstream actions or decisions.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are fed into Dify workflows without validation
IF Dify tools or agents act on summaries, classifications, or extracted facts from Chatwoot
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations back to original Chatwoot records
Limit Dify to read-only summarization for support content
Log and review all automated actions derived from Chatwoot
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Dify stores conversation logs and uploaded knowledge-base files and may send them to model providers. The pair therefore creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch on the same data class, especially if support content is copied into Dify. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the interaction, not either system alone.
conditions: IF customer support records are transferred from Chatwoot into Dify
IF Dify retention or provider residency differs from Chatwoot policy
mitigations: Classify which Chatwoot fields may enter Dify
Set a short retention window for Dify conversation logs
Restrict Dify providers to approved regions
Document a deletion/export workflow for transferred records
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
